texts.orig: Q: I’m a PM and I’m having a hard time getting buy-in for my ideas. My teammates quickly shoot me down, or disregard my recommendations. Any advice?
texts.text: Q: I’m a PM and I’m having a hard time getting buy-in for my ideas. My teammates quickly shoot me down, or disregard my recommendations. Any advice?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Buy-in is the lifeblood of Product Management. I learned this the hard way. As a new PM, I walked into my first roadmap planning meeting confident and excited. I was about to recommend that we build a new search feature, and I knew it was a slam-dunk idea.
texts.text: Buy-in is the lifeblood of Product Management. I learned this the hard way. As a new PM, I walked into my first roadmap planning meeting confident and excited. I was about to recommend that we build a new search feature, and I knew it was a slam-dunk idea.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: As I shared my recommendation with the product team, I was met with confused stares and irritated faces. After I was done, I was peppered with questions and comments: “Why should we prioritize this over another feature that’s easier to build?” and “I don’t get why we should offer this at all.”
texts.text: As I shared my recommendation with the product team, I was met with confused stares and irritated faces. After I was done, I was peppered with questions and comments: “Why should we prioritize this over another feature that’s easier to build?” and “I don’t get why we should offer this at all.”

texts.label: text
texts.orig: I left the meeting defeated and stressed. My team felt like I was forcing ideas on them and undervaluing their expertise.
texts.text: I left the meeting defeated and stressed. My team felt like I was forcing ideas on them and undervaluing their expertise.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This is a common problem, and one you can learn how to fix. I’ll let you in on the painfully obvious secret:
texts.text: This is a common problem, and one you can learn how to fix. I’ll let you in on the painfully obvious secret:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Buy-in is the result of showing your team why your idea achieves their goals
texts.text: Buy-in is the result of showing your team why your idea achieves their goals

texts.label: text
texts.orig: . It sounds trite, but it’s true.
texts.text: . It sounds trite, but it’s true.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In practice, however, it is difficult to do. In fact, over the years, I’ve realized there are three common reasons leaders fail to get buy-in. In this case, I was guilty of all three:
texts.text: In practice, however, it is difficult to do. In fact, over the years, I’ve realized there are three common reasons leaders fail to get buy-in. In this case, I was guilty of all three:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Assuming everyone is thinking what you’re thinking.
texts.text: Assuming everyone is thinking what you’re thinking.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: We assume the “right answer” must be obvious, but it almost never is.
texts.text: We assume the “right answer” must be obvious, but it almost never is.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: We believe there isn’t enough time to get everyone fully bought in before you have to move forward.
texts.text: We believe there isn’t enough time to get everyone fully bought in before you have to move forward.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: We’re afraid someone will dissent, so we try to sneak the plan through. Sometimes we do this subconsciously, and we aren’t even aware of this fear!
texts.text: We’re afraid someone will dissent, so we try to sneak the plan through. Sometimes we do this subconsciously, and we aren’t even aware of this fear!

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To avoid these pitfalls, I’ll share the three tactics that I’ve found to have the largest impact on getting buy-in:
texts.text: To avoid these pitfalls, I’ll share the three tactics that I’ve found to have the largest impact on getting buy-in:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If you co-create your idea with your team, your team will be infinitely more receptive to your suggestions. Co-creation means collaborating with others to identify the best solution or plan of action.
texts.text: If you co-create your idea with your team, your team will be infinitely more receptive to your suggestions. Co-creation means collaborating with others to identify the best solution or plan of action.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Co-creation is important for two reasons:
texts.text: Co-creation is important for two reasons:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: First, you create a better idea. Every day, you work with smart people with diverse perspectives. Leverage that! You don’t need to come up with the best idea; you need to execute on the best idea.
texts.text: First, you create a better idea. Every day, you work with smart people with diverse perspectives. Leverage that! You don’t need to come up with the best idea; you need to execute on the best idea.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Second, when you co-create, people feel invested in the idea, so they have a stake in the outcome.
texts.text: Second, when you co-create, people feel invested in the idea, so they have a stake in the outcome.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: After my failed attempt to rally my team around the feature I thought we should prioritize, I changed my approach and co-created with them. I walked them through the data, and we aligned on which part of the funnel had the biggest opportunity to improve conversion. They saw what I saw.
texts.text: After my failed attempt to rally my team around the feature I thought we should prioritize, I changed my approach and co-created with them. I walked them through the data, and we aligned on which part of the funnel had the biggest opportunity to improve conversion. They saw what I saw.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: We then brainstormed potential features and concluded, as a team, that we should prioritize building an improved search feature. In the end, we had a better solution than the one I initially proposed and everyone was bought in.
texts.text: We then brainstormed potential features and concluded, as a team, that we should prioritize building an improved search feature. In the end, we had a better solution than the one I initially proposed and everyone was bought in.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: You can co-create in practically any scenario: aligning with your team on quarterly OKRs, aligning with stakeholders on project status, asking for resources from a cross-functional partner, gaining support for your recommendation, or keeping a meeting on track.
texts.text: You can co-create in practically any scenario: aligning with your team on quarterly OKRs, aligning with stakeholders on project status, asking for resources from a cross-functional partner, gaining support for your recommendation, or keeping a meeting on track.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: It’s so common to start working on a project and do everything yourself before talking to others. This is shortsighted! Again, your goal isn’t to come up with a great idea; it is to execute on a great idea. So once you have a straw-man proposal to tackle a problem, bring together the group that’s affected. Run a brainstorming session to jointly iterate on the draft proposal and align on what success looks like. That will get everyone’s brain churning and help you co-create. Stakeholders will feel valued. You’ll stop hearing “I wish you’d looped us in earlier.”
texts.text: It’s so common to start working on a project and do everything yourself before talking to others. This is shortsighted! Again, your goal isn’t to come up with a great idea; it is to execute on a great idea. So once you have a straw-man proposal to tackle a problem, bring together the group that’s affected. Run a brainstorming session to jointly iterate on the draft proposal and align on what success looks like. That will get everyone’s brain churning and help you co-create. Stakeholders will feel valued. You’ll stop hearing “I wish you’d looped us in earlier.”

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Show your work while you work.
texts.text: Show your work while you work.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Remember math class where your teacher would require you to show the process of solving the problem, instead of just writing down the solution? Take “show your work” one step further. As you are coming up with ideas and thinking through the problem, get used to sharing updates along the way. You can do this by dropping a summary of user interview results in Slack or sharing learnings and challenges in casual conversations in between meetings or formal weekly check-ins.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: It’s easy to mentally write off a stakeholder who expresses concerns about your idea. You may think, “They just don’t get it.” This gets you nowhere. Invest the time to understand people’s concerns and motivations. Ask open-ended questions to gain insights to create a compelling pitch. Questions include:

Invest the time to understand people’s concerns and motivations. Ask open-ended questions to gain insights to create a compelling pitch. Questions include:

texts.orig: Presence is an elusive trait. We know it when we see it. It’s our ability to own the room. The
texts.text: Presence is an elusive trait. We know it when we see it. It’s our ability to own the room. The

texts.label: text
texts.orig: describes it as “your ability to project mature self-confidence; a sense that you can take control of difficult, unpredictable situations, make tough decisions in a timely way, and hold your own with other talented and strong-willed team members.”
texts.text: describes it as “your ability to project mature self-confidence; a sense that you can take control of difficult, unpredictable situations, make tough decisions in a timely way, and hold your own with other talented and strong-willed team members.”

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Presence is important because it shapes how colleagues perceive us. This impacts our ability to influence.
texts.text: Presence is important because it shapes how colleagues perceive us. This impacts our ability to influence.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Presence is a combination of verbal cues, body language, and mindset. One of the actions you can take to improve your presence is to stop saying “sorry” when it’s not warranted. texts.label: text
texts.orig: Natalie, a senior engineer at Salesforce, realized she said “sorry” all the time when we were discussing this in the Arise Leadership Accelerator. She practiced not saying it as her default response. Within a week, her team commented that she presented more compelling ideas and showed up stronger. A seemingly simple change can have a powerful impact.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In addition, own your voice by getting rid of qualifiers like “actually,” “quickly,” or “just.” For example: “I actually have an idea,” “I just think that…” or “I have a quick question.”
texts.text: In addition, own your voice by getting rid of qualifiers like “actually,” “quickly,” or “just.” For example: “I actually have an idea,” “I just think that…” or “I have a quick question.”

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: “Just” demeans what you have to say. It shrinks your power and influence.
texts.text: “Just” demeans what you have to say. It shrinks your power and influence.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: “Actually” communicates a sense of surprise that you have something to contribute.
texts.text: “Actually” communicates a sense of surprise that you have something to contribute.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: “Quickly” assumes by default you’re imposing on others.
texts.text: “Quickly” assumes by default you’re imposing on others.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Don’t minimize yourself. Trust yourself—share your ideas and ask the questions.
texts.text: Don’t minimize yourself. Trust yourself—share your ideas and ask the questions.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: One big reason we fail to get buy-in is that we assume everyone else is thinking what we’re thinking. Storytelling helps break through this roadblock.
texts.text: One big reason we fail to get buy-in is that we assume everyone else is thinking what we’re thinking. Storytelling helps break through this roadblock.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Good storytelling means you present a narrative that resonates with your audience.
texts.text: Good storytelling means you present a narrative that resonates with your audience.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Focus on why stakeholders should care about the idea.
texts.text: Focus on why stakeholders should care about the idea.

texts.orig: For example, prioritizing a recommendation feature will improve conversion or changing the sprint process will free up time to reduce tech debt.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To drive alignment, always focus on co-creating, showcasing presence, and storytelling. It’s an ongoing process. The more you practice, the more natural it will get. Influencing is the best way to drive a larger impact at your company and move up faster in your career. Good luck and happy influencing!
